title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: the subject is truncated Barsotti–Tate groups of level 1 (killed by p) over a base S of characteristic p, and how they relate to their Dieudonné data. On S we have a locally free module M (the Dieudonné module evaluated on S, M = ε*(𝓜)), with F_M : M^(p) → M and V_M : M → M^(p), where M^(p) is the Frobenius pullback. These satisfy Ker F = Im V and Ker V = Im F, so they form an exact sequence. M carries the Hodge filtration 0 → ω → M → t' → 0 with ω and t' locally free. On the previous page Grothendieck shows ω^(p) = Im(V_M) ⊂ M^(p) and t'^(p) = Coker(V_M). Hence the triple (M, F, V) alone determines the Hodge filtration.

This page draws two squares, then a cross diagram.

(1) First square. Since V_M has image ω^(p), it factors as M → ω^(p) ⊂ M^(p). Restricting to ω ⊂ M gives a map V_ω : ω → ω^(p). This is the Verschiebung/Hasse–Witt map on the cotangent space.

(2) Second square. Since F_M kills Im V_M, it factors through Coker V_M = t'^(p), giving t'^(p) → M. Composing with the projection M → t' gives F_{t'} : t'^(p) → t'. Its transpose is V_{ω'} on the dual ω' = t'^∨.

(3) Cross diagram. The horizontal row is the Hodge filtration 0 → ω → M → t' → 0. The vertical column is 0 → t'^(p) → M → ω^(p) → 0, the 'conjugate' filtration given by Im F = Ker V. It is exact because F is injective on Coker V and V is surjective onto Im V = ω^(p). The two diagonals record that
- the composite ω → M → ω^(p) equals V_ω;
- the composite t'^(p) → M → t' equals F_{t'}.

The purpose, posed as a question on the previous page, is whether (M, F_M, V_M) recovers the whole 'donnée b)'. The answer sketched here: from (M, F, V) one reconstructs the Hodge filtration, the conjugate filtration, the Frobenius-twisted identification of their graded pieces, and the induced maps V_ω, F_{t'}. In modern terms, a BT_1 over a char-p base gives an F-zip structure on M (Moonen–Wedhorn) via two transversal-in-the-graded-sense filtrations. The two-filtration cross diagram is the linear-algebra picture behind the classification of BT_1's and the Ekedahl–Oort stratification.
errors: No mathematical error. Exactness of the vertical sequence silently uses that M, ω, t' are locally free and that Ker F = Im V and Ker V = Im F hold on the evaluated module. This was assumed on the previous page.

The horizontal arrows in the two squares are drawn ambiguously. The natural maps are the inclusions ω ⊂ M and ω^(p) ⊂ M^(p), and the projections M → t' and M^(p) → t'^(p) = Coker V_M. 'M → ω' cannot be a canonical map as written.

ideas.what: Factorization of V_M through ω^(p) = Im V_M, giving V_ω : ω → ω^(p) (Hasse–Witt/Verschiebung on the cotangent space)
ideas.modern_name: Hasse–Witt map / Verschiebung on Lie algebra dual
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hasse–Witt; Oda 1969 for the Dieudonné/de Rham comparison)
ideas.where_published: Possibly Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970, publ. 1974); unsure of exact form

ideas.what: Factorization of F_M through t'^(p) = Coker V_M, giving F_{t'} : t'^(p) → t' and its transpose V_{ω'}
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius on the tangent space / duality of Hasse–Witt maps

ideas.what: Cross diagram combining the Hodge filtration (ω ⊂ M) with the conjugate filtration (t'^(p) = Im F ⊂ M), with the diagonals giving V_ω and F_{t'}; the triple (M, F, V) determines everything
ideas.modern_name: F-zip structure on the Dieudonné module of a BT_1 (Hodge vs. conjugate filtration)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kraft (1975, unpublished), Oort, Moonen (2001), Moonen–Wedhorn (2004, F-zips)
ideas.where_published: Not in this explicit form to my knowledge; Montréal lectures treat BT_n and Dieudonné crystals more generally

missed.claim: Over an arbitrary char-p base, Grothendieck organizes the level-1 Dieudonné module as two filtrations: the Hodge filtration (row) and the Im F = Ker V filtration (column). These are linked by Frobenius-twisted identifications of their graded pieces. This is essentially the F-zip formalism later used for Ekedahl–Oort strata. The note suggests the linear-algebra structure was already in view around 1970, but it is a sketch only.
missed.quote: On aura 0 → t'^(p) → … 0 → ω → M → t' → 0 … V_ω ↘ ω^(p)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority context for F-zips and EO stratification (Kraft/Oort/Moonen–Wedhorn). It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard Hodge/conjugate filtration picture for Dieudonné modules of BT_1's. It is mildly interesting as an early, base-general sketch anticipating the F-zip viewpoint, but it is routine and fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: Second square: the top-left object should be M, not M^(p). The vertical arrow is F_M : M^(p) → M (pointing up), and the diagonal arrow goes from t'^(p) up to M (the factorization of F_M).

First square: the horizontal arrows should be read as inclusions ω ↪ M and ω^(p) ↪ M^(p). The diagonal M → ω^(p) is the factorization of V_M through its image. Its label '[?]' is unclear and likely just names this factorization, not 'φ_1'.
Second square: the horizontal arrows are the projections M → t' and M^(p) → t'^(p).
